title: sse: fix partial-JSON delimiter ordering and token/event framing in streaming responses
author: Anya Patel
release_notes: Fixes streaming SSE chunking and framing bugs that caused malformed partial JSON and out-of-order token/event emissions during OpenAI-compat streaming. Backwards compatible and no breaking changes.
description: Summary: Fix ordering and framing bugs in SSE streaming that caused partial JSON fragments, missing delimiters, and token/event interleaving that broke OpenAI-compatible streaming clients. Motivation: Several downstream customers and the internal integration test suite observed flakiness when receiving streamed structured output or function-calling JSON across high-latency networks; partial JSON objects could be emitted with delimiter bytes out-of-order or with token events flushed before framing boundaries which caused parsers to see malformed JSON. Root cause: two races in the streaming code path. 1) The chunker emitted chunk boundaries and delimiter tokens independently of the JSON emitter flush semantics, which allowed network-sized chunks to split logical delimiters across TCP frames. 2) The token/event emitter could schedule token events (text/event-stream tokens) ahead of a final framing delimiter for partial JSON objects when the KV-cache or batching path triggered mid-generation. Fixes implemented: reorder delimiter emission so that the SSE delimiter/newline is always emitted atomically before any token/event payload for a given logical message; introduce a minimal reassembly buffer and deterministic flush policy in runtime/streaming/chunker.py to coalesce byte-level partial fragments when a logical delimiter appears split across network chunks; add a short-lived boundary marker at the adapter layer (openai/compat/streaming_adapter.go) that guarantees adapters see complete delimiter sequences before converting events to the OpenAI streaming format; ensure that structured output (function-calling JSON) is emitted with a finalizing event after all partial tokens are delivered. Compatibility: All changes are backward compatible with the existing SSE and OpenAI-compat streaming APIs. The OpenAI compatibility adapter preserves old event shapes and only changes emission ordering to be deterministic. Performance: microbenchmarks show <1% p95 latency overhead in worst-case scenarios; throughput is unaffected in steady-state. Tests: Added deterministic unit tests covering split-delimiter cases and delayed-chunk arrival, integration test that simulates high-latency chunking and confirms client JSON reassembly, and compatibility tests exercising SDK clients in Python and TypeScript. Author (Anya): "Added test case runtime/tests/test_sse_partial_json.py::test_three_chunk_split and extended the integration harness to simulate packetization; details in commit c3d4e5f." Priya Singh: "Are there any SDK-level changes required?" Anya: "No API changes; SDKs receive the same SSE shape. I added a small helper in the Python SDK to ease tests but left public surface unchanged." Katherine Moore: "CI flakes were seen in the first run; rerun after fixing a timing issue." CI: initial pipeline failed on flaky integration tests (timeout in sse high-latency job), reran the sse-tests job after adding deterministic timing control in tests; final CI status: pass. Approvals: Marcus Liu approved after tests were added, Priya Singh approved, Katherine Moore gave final approval. Merge: Squash merged to main on 2026-02-22 by Anya Patel. Notes for ops: No rollout or migration steps required. If customers report regressions, revert by reverting commit a1b2c3d and follow up with ENG-3423 for a hotfix.
